matt_w: Heads up 30 canary with spec-decoding + aggressive pruning (prune=0.6) + q4 brought up a weird mismatch: ~0.4% of requests return truncated responses or OOMs.
lina: yikes. repro on stage or only in canary?
matt_w: only in canary so far, ~3500 reqs, 14 failures. patterns look like token_stream length off-by-one after speculative merge.
talia: any stack traces? runtime logs?
benchbot: attached quick run: model=ember-7b-q4-pruned0.6, speculative=true, spec_ratio=0.6, runs=3500
benchbot: summary: failures=14 (0.4%), median_lat=95ms, p95=420ms (spec enabled), tps=220 tok/s, mem_peak=13.6GB
benchbot: sample failure snippet:
```
[ERROR] speculative/merge.cpp:142 merge_size_mismatch: expected 48 got 47
callstack: runtime::spec_merge() -> runtime::apply_kvcache() -> alloc_temp_buf()
```
matt_w: that merge_size_mismatch smells like cache-length not matching when we drop pruned tokens.
omar: pruning changes tokenization alignment? maybe our prune pipeline was applied post-tokenize differently between spec and main path.
lina: good point. speculative actor uses a lighter tokenizer path for perf, could be skipping a normalization step.
talia: can we reproduce locally with a deterministic seed? if so, we can diff KV states pre/post merge.
matt_w: I ran a deterministic run: seed=42, input=long-doc-12k, speculative warm=8. repros reliably on that input.
benchbot: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-test-artifacts/spec-prune/6100000000/{logs,diffs,core_dumps}.tar.gz
omar: quick mitigation: disable pruning on speculative candidate path (keep full logits). That should align sizes, albeit with perf cost.
lina: do we accept perf regression to avoid correctness failures? can we selectively disable pruning only when spec is active?
talia: yes, patch runtime to fallback: if speculative && pruning_enabled -> run unpruned candidate generation.
matt_w: also add an assert that checks merge buffer sizes and logs token ids on mismatch before failing, so we get better triage data.
devops-bot: rolling patch to spec-runtime v1.3.2-pre1 queued for staging deploy.
benchbot: quick experiment after disabling pruning on spec-path: runs=3600, failures=0, median_lat=112ms, p95=460ms, tps=200 tok/s, mem_peak=14.1GB
matt_w: perf hit but acceptable for canary. we should gate canary on zero merge failures and re-run smoke quality.
omar: followup items: (1) runtime guard + logging PR, (2) adjust onboarding harness to run long-doc inputs under spec/prune combos, (3) add unit test for merge size invariants.
lina: I'll file the runtime PR and include the assert + telemetry counters.
talia: I'll update the onboarding checklist to add a "spec+prune" matrix test with a couple long-form prompts.
benchbot: QA notes: sampling KL to baseline stayed low (0.012) on smoke set; halluc flag delta +0.4% (within noise).
omar: long-term we should coordinate tokenizer normalization between prune pipeline and spec actor so we don't hold this fallback forever.
matt_w: agreed. good triage. leaving canary paused until staging patch goes through.
lina: thanks 2 team — keeping this documented in the spec-decode runbook. :white_check_mark:
